_: ONE table for how a design note's or a spec's TITLE is read (docs/hub/design.md, "The file", the title row and "How the title is read"; #147), read by both readers of it: Scripts/Read-DesignTree.ps1 Get-P20DesignTitle (tkTestToolkit -Design) and agent/ado/design.py parse_doc / doc_title (Tests/test_design.py). Each row's lines are joined with LF, or CRLF when crlf is true, into the file's text; name is the file's name; expected is the title the Design tab lists it under. The rule, in order: the FIRST heading after the frontmatter, when it is level one (# ); else the first non-empty line after the first '## Title' heading, unless that line is itself a heading; else the file's name. A level-one heading after any other heading is a sentence in the body, not the title. If the two halves ever disagree about a row, one of them is wrong.

rows.name: the design contract template: '## Title', the title on the next line
lines: The Gym Where the Models Work Out
rows.expected: The Gym Where the Models Work Out

rows.name: a level-one heading before any other heading: the title, as before
lines: description: "What the board could show next"

rows.name: the only level-one heading is deep in the body: the file's name, not that sentence
lines: Two roommates and a server rack.

rows.name: neither a leading level-one heading nor a '## Title' section: the file's name
'## Title' ahead of a deep level-one heading: the Title section wins
the contract template in a CRLF file
lines: The Gym Where the Models Work Out
rows.expected: The Gym Where the Models Work Out

rows.name: an empty '## Title' section: the next heading is not a title, so the file's name
